column1: # The tests tools/ios-device-test.sh does not run as they stand on the acceptance iPhone, each with its reason.
# A line is seven tab-separated fields, `-` where a field does not apply:
#   package <TAB> cargo target <TAB> test <TAB> kind <TAB> child test <TAB> child environment <TAB> why
# The target is the name cargo gives the test binary (a library's is its crate name, an integration test's its
# file name), and the test is its full name as the harness lists it. The kinds:
#   host-path  the test reads a path of the machine that built it (a CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR path), which a phone
#              does not hold. It is left out, and the host's own run of the same test is its check.
#   rerun      the test starts its own binary again as a child process (craftbridge_process::rerun), which an
#              iOS app cannot do: it has no way to start a process. The runner runs the child test itself, in
#              an app launch of its own, with the environment the parent's call gives its child (NAME=value
#              words, or `-` for none), so the child's own assertions run on the phone in a process that has
#              the environment from its start, which is all the parent exists to arrange. The child field
#              names the `#[ignore]`d test the parent reruns; no other kind has a child or an environment.
#   host-tool  the test starts a program of the machine that built it (cargo, rustc, mkfifo, the EffectCraft
#              command line the conformance stage builds), which a phone does not hold and an iOS app could not
#              start. The test field `*` names every test of a binary such a program drives from its first
#              line, which the runner then does not install.
# The runner refuses, before it builds anything, a line that is not this shape: another number of fields, an
# empty one, another kind, no reason, or a rerun's child missing. It refuses a line whose test the binary does
# not list, or whose name is part of another test's (the harness skips by part of a name), so a rename cannot
# leave a test quietly unrun (a `*` line is not checked, since it names no test).
